newsitem.title: USA: 3M sale makes Outdoor Systems a U.S. giant.
newsitem.headline: 3M sale makes Outdoor Systems a U.S. giant.

text.p: Outdoor Systems Inc. agreed to buy National Advertising Co. for $1 billion from 3M, the companies said Thursday, strengthening its position as the nation's largest billboard advertising company.
Based in Phoenix, Ariz., Outdoor Systems will have 96,000 billboards and other signs after the deal, an increase of more than 50 percent, and will reach into 40 states, up from 25.
Outdoor Systems may have to sell billboards or other assets in some markets so the deal can win approval from regulators, company officials said.
"There are anywhere from five to 10 markets where (antitrust regulation) may be an issue," a spokeswoman for Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co. said.
"Outdoor Systems has proposed to sell some of its boards in those markets. That's part of the plan."
Outdoor Systems' biggest markets include Los Angeles, Chicago, Detroit and Houston.

When it bought the outdoor advertising business of Gannett Co. for $710 million last year, the Justice Department required a review of its Houston holdings, an Outdoor Systems spokesman said. Similar reviews were likely from the 3M deal, he said.
For St. Paul, Minn.-based 3M, the deal is another step as it sells off non-core assets. Last July, it spun off its data storage and imaging businesses into a new company called Imation Corp.

"This does look like an additional example of pruning the portfolio," said Schroder Wertheim analyst Michael Ellman regarding the outdoor advertising business sale. "This was a valuable asset, but not one that was core to 3M's business."
3M stock fell 12.5 cents to $86.875 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Outdoor Systems rose $1.625 to $29.375 on Nasdaq.
The price that Outdoor Systems agreed to pay for the 3M business was rich considering that it had annual revenues of $220 million, analysts said.
One of the big issues facing the outdoor advertising business is potential restriction of tobacco ads, which still comprise a sizable portion of U.S. billboard space.
But 3M had reduced its tobacco ads to 4 percent of its total outdoor advertising revenue and was on track to eliminate it entirely by 1998, it said.
Outdoor Systems said it still has tobacco clients, but that its revenues from them have declined as well.
